glosses: slam
Annonce par le preneur qu’il compte réaliser toutes les levées d’une partie (grand chelem) ou toutes moins une (petit chelem).

examples.text: Il y est allé avec le "petit" septième, les quatre rois et trois dames mais on avait préparé la donne pour qu’il subisse un chelem mémorable.
Employé adjectivement dans les expressions: Être chelem, faire chelem: ne pas faire un seul pli.

glosses: Action de remporter toutes les victoires d’une compétition sportive.

examples.text: Il peut toujours rêver à un exceptionnel grand chelem, c'est-à-dire une victoire dans chacune des six épreuves.
L'équipe de France de rugby à XV a réussi un grand chelem (cinq victoires en cinq matchs) dans le Tournoi des six nations en 2002, 2004, 2010 et 2022

glosses: To shut with sudden force so as to produce a shock and noise.

examples.text: Don't slam the door!
Britain’s borders: wide open to Covid, slammed shut for people in need [title]

glosses: To put in or on a particular place with force and loud noise. (Often followed by a preposition such as down, against or into.)

examples.text: Don't slam that trunk down on the pavement!
The New South Wales police commissioner has defended the officer who was filmed slamming an Indigenous boy face-first on to a pavement in Sydney, saying the officer “had a bad day”.

glosses: To strike forcefully with some implement.

examples.text: But Wolves went in front when Steven Fletcher headed in Stephen Hunt's cross and it was 2-0 when Geoffrey Mujangi Bia slammed in his first for the club.

glosses: To strike against suddenly and heavily.

examples.text: The boat slammed into the bank and we were almost thrown into the river.
The 6-ton fishing boat Kuanghua 15638 was slammed by the communist vessel near the Liuchuan reefs off the coast of Chukuang and drifted toward Nanchu after the collision.
Seven people were killed and 66 injured after a High Speed Train slammed into a stationary vehicle that had been parked across the main line by a suicidal driver.

glosses: To strike and take the life of or at least incapacitate for some time.

examples.text:

glosses: To defeat or overcome in a match.

examples.text: The Armenian football team has slammed the Turks 6–0.

glosses: To speak badly of; to criticize forcefully.

examples.text: Critics slammed the new film, calling it violent and meaningless.

glosses: To clean (a surface) by means of a stroking motion of a broom or brush.

examples.text: to sweep a floor, the street, or a chimney
I will sweep it with the besom of destruction.

glosses: To move through a (horizontal) arc or similar long stroke.

examples.text: The wind sweeps across the plain.
The offended countess swept out of the ballroom.
[H]as the course of the argument so accustomed you to agreeing that you were swept by it into a ready assent?

glosses: To search (a place) methodically.
To travel quickly.

examples.text: Drifting thus, we made fast time down the bank through Cove Bay, and at 72 m.p.h. came sweeping round the curve past Girdleness light house, and so to the first sight of Aberdeen itself.

glosses: To play a sweep shot.

To defeat (a team) in a series without drawing or losing any of the games in that series.

examples.text: And like a peacock sweep along his tail.

glosses: To vacuum a carpet or rug.

examples.text: Give the front steps a quick sweep to get rid of those fallen leaves.

glosses: The person who steers a dragon boat.

glosses: A methodical search, typically for bugs (electronic listening devices).

examples.text: Bradman attempted a sweep, but in fact top edged the ball to the wicket keeper

glosses: A lottery, usually on the results of a sporting event, where players win if their randomly chosen team wins.

examples.text: Jim will win fifty dollars in the office sweep if Japan wins the World Cup.

glosses: A flow of water parallel to shore caused by wave action at an ocean beach or at a point or headland.

examples.text: The MiG-17's inner wing has 45 degrees of sweep.

glosses: A throw or takedown that primarily uses the legs to attack an opponent's legs.
Violent and general destruction.

examples.text: the sweep of an epidemic disease

glosses: A movable template for making moulds, in loam moulding.

examples.text: the road which makes a small sweep

glosses: A rowing style in which each rower rows with oar on either the port or starboard side.

examples.text: I am primarily a sweep rower.
